hints.content:
The expression for $g(x)$ includes a logarithmic term.

Remember that the derivative of the general logarithmic term $\log_a(x)$ (where $a$ is any positive constant and $a\neq 1$) is $\dfrac{1}{\ln(a)\cdot x}$.

Put another way, $\dfrac{d}{dx}[\log_a(x)]=\dfrac{1}{\ln(a)\cdot x}$.

[[☃ explanation 2]]

options.explanation:
Not everyone will find this useful, but here's our suggestion:

The derivative of $\ln(x)$ is simply $\dfrac{1}{x}$:

$\dfrac{d}{dx}[\ln(x)]=\dfrac{1}{x}$

According to the change of base rule, we can rewrite $\log_a(x)$ for any base $a$ as the quotient of two natural logarithms:

$\log_a(x)=\dfrac{\ln(x)}{\ln(a)}$

This way, we can differentiate any logarithmic term as follows:

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{d}{dx}[\log_a(x)]&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{\ln(x)}{\ln(a)}\right]
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\ln(a)}\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}[\ln(x)]
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\ln(a)}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}
\\\\
&=\dfrac{1}{\ln(a)\cdot x}
\end{align}$
